To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The leading pion in a quark jet is preferentially polarized along its direction of motion, (2) the transverse polarization of the leading pion in quark jet is opposite to the transverse momentum of the jet, and (3) the leading pion is preferentially polarizd in the plane of the jet.

the polarization of the two leading pion in a jet produced in the fragmentation of a transversely polarized quark is proportional to the transverse polarization of the quark and the correlation of the polarizations of the two pions is proportional to the product of the two transverse polarizations of the quark.

1) we have computed polarization asymmetries for the two leading pion correlations in a quark jet, 2) these asymmetries are non-vanishing and are sensitive to the details of the quark--pseudoscalar meson interactions, 3) these asymmetriess can be measured in the near future at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider, 4) they can be used to study chiral symmetry breaking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of chiral symmetry in QCD, and its manifestations in hadron physics.
the question of whether there is any evidence for a chiral anomaly in the quark fragmentation process.
the study of the chiral dynamics of quark fragmentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the linear sigma model is an effective theory for quark--pionic correlations in polarized fragmentation, and that this model can be used to compute polarization observables in quark fragmentation.
the pion--pion correlation asymmetry is a very sensitive probe to chiral symmetry breaking.
the pion--pion correlation asymmetry is an observable that can provide information about the chiral symmetry of QCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chiral symmetry breaking effects in quark fragmentation can be observed in the pi pi correlations.
the chiral symmetry breaking is the origin of quark polarization in the fragmentation.
we have shown that the chiral symmetry breaking effects in quark fragmentation can be observed in the correlation between pions in the jet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarization asymmetries are large and can be measured at the LHC.
the asymmetry in the pi - pi correlations depends on the relative orientation of the transverse quark polarization vector with respect to the transverse momentum vector of the leading pion.
the polarization of quarks in the fragmentation process is a promising probe of the chiral dynamics of QCD.
